business_model: Individual/small-group health insurance carrier with a consumer-tech-forward member experience

historical_evidence.company: Founded 2012 by Josh Kushner, Mario Schlosser, and Kevin Nazemi, a health-insurance company built to offer ACA-marketplace individual and small-group plans with a modern, app-driven member experience.
historical_evidence.market: Large but heavily regulated, capital-intensive, and structurally difficult insurance market with thin margins and significant underwriting risk — a fundamentally different risk profile than a typical software marketplace.
historical_evidence.team: Founder Josh Kushner had a notable venture-investing background (Thrive Capital); the team had scaled the company through several large funding rounds by the snapshot date.
historical_evidence.product: Modern, app-based member experience layered on top of a traditional insurance-carrier operating model — the technology layer was genuinely differentiated from legacy insurers, but the underlying insurance-underwriting economics are the harder, more consequential part of the business.
historical_evidence.execution: Raised $400M in Series C funding in February 2016, led by Fidelity, at a $2.7B valuation — a roughly $1B valuation increase from a $1.7B valuation just five months earlier (September 2015, $32.5M from Google Capital), an unusually large and fast valuation step-up.
historical_evidence.traction: No specific member-count figures were found in the contemporaneous sources reviewed for the February 2016 snapshot.
historical_evidence.financial: Contemporaneous coverage explicitly reported significant underwriting losses as the company scaled, alongside the large valuation increase — a genuine, real-time-visible tension between rapid growth/valuation momentum and reported financial losses, rather than a retrospective judgment.

sources.title: Oscar Health Gets $400 Million And A $2.7 Billion Valuation from Fidelity
